instrument.note: AT-D3-1's instrument half: `fx-snapshot-4` alone, then silence. No message is delivered at all, which is what makes *no `edge` row* and *no `phase: left` row* claims about a correct client rather than about an empty run.

clean_finish.note: AT-D3-2's DISCRIMINATING CONTROL: `aimla-impl-1`, whose `fx-snapshot-4` state is `working`, driven to a CLEAN `turn.end` — D2 § 4.3 rule 4's `stop_hook` end reason with a zero aborted count, which is the only rule that produces `idle`. So the test measures the `/clear` trace and not the absence of an idle render anywhere.

ages_dark_desks.note: fx-snapshot-4 with aimla-impl-2 stale (silent 11m) and aimla-review offline (silent 2h 06m), so the dark-only receipt age renders on two desks and not on the two live ones; and every context.sampled_received_at is BEFORE server_time, unlike D2 § 8.2.2's worked snapshot (14:41:04.880Z against 14:23:14.400Z), so the gauge age is non-zero and discriminates. D2's contradiction is recorded on card#7341, not edited here.

badge_raise.note: FLOOR § 6.2 A11 (badge-raise), which no other run exercises (card#7341 step 6 review, carried to step 8): `fx-snapshot-4`, then three deltas for `aimla-impl-2` that each carry `badges` in `changed[]`. The first GAINS `lossy` (A11 fires, once, caused by 20545); the second RE-SENDS the same array (`changed[]` carries `badges` and nothing is gained, so a predicate that fired on the member alone would fire here); the third DROPS it (a loss, which A11's condition names as no animation). Exactly one A11 row is correct, and both a never-firing and an always-firing row are distinguishable from it.

feed_dies.note: AT-D3-6's floor half: `fx-snapshot-4`, the on-connect `fleet.health`, heartbeats at D2's 15 s cadence for 60 s, then nothing for 60 s more. The viewer clock starts at 14:23:30 (`browser_clock_ms`), so the four heartbeats land at 14:23:45, 14:24:00, 14:24:15 and 14:24:30 and cross exactly one minute boundary, and the silence spans 14:25:00. Every poll the client issues during the silence is ANSWERED with a current snapshot (`clocked`), which is what exercises § 6.5's *a poll sets nothing*.

feed_lives.note: AT-D3-6's discriminating control: the same run with a heartbeat every 15 s for the whole 120 s, so the feed never dies, no poll is issued, and the wall clock advances on the heartbeats that cross 14:24:00 and 14:25:00 and on no other.

unrecognised.note: AT-D3-11: `fx-snapshot-4`, then a `render_state` of "pondering" on `aimla-impl-2` (twice — the second delivery re-sends the same value, so *once per distinct value* can fail), a badge "quantum_flux" on `aimla-impl-1`, and an `unknown_reason` of "reasons" on `aimla-pm`. `aimla-review` is untouched: it is the desk *no other desk is affected* is asserted on.

lobby_intact.note: AT-D3-15's discriminating control (card#7341 step 9): fx-snapshot-4 intact, and two heartbeats that agree with it. The lobby renders no discrepancy notice and the protocol issues no fetch beyond the connect read.

lobby_short.note: AT-D3-15, N < M (card#7341 step 9): the client missed aimla-review's insert, because its connect snapshot predates the seat, and the heartbeat's seats_total is one higher than the seats it holds. The protocol issues one discovery fetch, after which the counts agree. The second heartbeat agrees and fetches nothing.

lobby_over.note: AT-D3-15, N > M (card#7341 step 9): the client missed aimla-review's seat.retired, so it holds four desks while the heartbeat's seats_total is three. The protocol issues one discovery fetch, and since card#7342 step 10 its rows REMOVE the desk they omit (FLOOR § 2.3 row 4's full-snapshot backstop), so the counts agree once it lands and the SECOND IDENTICAL heartbeat issues no fetch.

lobby_short_fails.note: FLOOR § 4.1 (card#7341 step 9): a discovery fetch that fails spends nothing, so the next heartbeat carrying the same (N, M) retries it, and the retry resolves the disagreement.

lobby_short_inflight.note: FLOOR § 4.1 (card#7341 step 9): one discovery fetch is in flight at a time. The discovery for (3, 4) answers 20 s after it was issued, so the second heartbeat lands while it is in flight, carrying a DIFFERENT pair, (3, 5), which the budget has never spent, and it issues nothing. Only the in-flight rule stops it. When the discovery lands, its newer fleet{} agrees with the seats it delivered.

lobby_discovers_room.note: Appendix B row 9 (card#7341 step 9): a discovery fetch adds a whole install, aimla-win and its two seats, and the client's record carries the membership lines the lobby renders. The discovery body is fx-membership leg_c's.

lobby_cold_silent.note: FLOOR § 4.1's silence (card#7341 step 9): the connect snapshot fails and nothing re-runs the client, so no check can ever run for the pair a heartbeat reports. The page carries § 9's failure render and the disagreement line says nothing.
